subject: maths
topicDisplay: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Use scale drawings and map scales
Divide a quantity in a given ratio
Find a percentage of an amount
Use compound units (speed, density, unit pricing)

questions.q: Convert 3.6 km into metres.
questions.explain: A metre is smaller than a kilometre, so multiply by 1000: 3.6 × 1000 = 3600 m.

questions.q: A jug holds 2.5 litres. How many millilitres is that?

questions.lo: Use scale drawings and map scales
questions.q: A map uses a scale of 1 cm : 5 km. Two places are 8 cm apart on the map. What is the real distance?
questions.explain: Each 1 cm represents 5 km, so 8 × 5 = 40 km.

questions.lo: Use scale drawings and map scales
questions.q: A model car is built to a scale of 1 : 50. What does this scale tell you?
options: The real car is 50 cm long
The real car is 50 times bigger than the model
The model is 50 times bigger than the real car
The real car is 50 cm bigger than the model
questions.explain: In a scale 1 : 50, every 1 unit on the model represents 50 of the same units in real life, so the real car is 50 times bigger.

questions.q: Write the ratio 18 : 24 in its simplest form.
questions.explain: The highest common factor of 18 and 24 is 6. Dividing both parts by 6 gives 3 : 4.

questions.q: Squash and water are mixed in the ratio 1 : 4. What fraction of the drink is squash?
questions.explain: A ratio is not a fraction of the whole. The parts add to 1 + 4 = 5, so squash is 1 out of 5 parts = 1/5.

questions.lo: Divide a quantity in a given ratio
questions.q: Share £48 in the ratio 3 : 5. How much is the smaller share?
questions.explain: Total parts = 3 + 5 = 8. One part = 48 ÷ 8 = £6. The smaller share is 3 parts = 3 × 6 = £18.

questions.lo: Divide a quantity in a given ratio
questions.q: A 60 cm ribbon is cut in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. How long is the longest piece?
questions.explain: Total parts = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. One part = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 cm. The longest piece is 3 parts = 3 × 10 = 30 cm.

questions.q: 5 identical pencils cost £1.75. How much do 8 of the same pencils cost?
questions.explain: One pencil = 1.75 ÷ 5 = £0.35. Then 8 × 0.35 = £2.80 (unitary method).

questions.q: Which graph shows two quantities in direct proportion?
options: A straight line through the origin (0, 0)
A straight line crossing the y-axis above zero
questions.explain: Directly proportional quantities give a straight line that passes through the origin, because when one is zero so is the other.

questions.q: It takes 4 builders 9 days to build a wall. How long would 6 builders take, working at the same rate?
questions.explain: This is inverse proportion. Total work = 4 × 9 = 36 builder-days. Time = 36 ÷ 6 = 6 days.

questions.q: Which situation is an example of inverse proportion?
options: More litres of petrol cost more money
More people sharing a fixed cake means each gets less
More hours worked means more pay
More metres of fabric means more cost
questions.explain: In inverse proportion, as one quantity increases the other decreases. Sharing a fixed cake among more people gives each person less.

questions.lo: Find a percentage of an amount
questions.q: Find 35% of 80.
questions.explain: 35% = 0.35 as a multiplier, so 0.35 × 80 = 28.

questions.q: A coat costing £60 is reduced by 25% in a sale. What is the sale price?
questions.explain: A 25% decrease means a multiplier of 0.75, so 0.75 × 60 = £45.

questions.q: A price rises from £40 to £50. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explain: Percentage change = change ÷ original × 100. The change is £10, so 10 ÷ 40 × 100 = 25% (divide by the ORIGINAL, not the new price).

questions.q: £600 is saved at 4% simple interest per year. How much interest is earned after 3 years?
questions.explain: One year's interest = 0.04 × 600 = £24. With simple interest the same amount is added each year: 24 × 3 = £72.

questions.lo: Use compound units (speed, density, unit pricing)
questions.q: A cyclist travels 45 km in 3 hours. What is the average speed?
questions.explain: Speed = distance ÷ time = 45 ÷ 3 = 15 km/h.

questions.lo: Use compound units (speed, density, unit pricing)
questions.q: A block has mass 150 g and volume 50 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explain: Density = mass ÷ volume = 150 ÷ 50 = 3 g/cm³.

questions.lo: Use compound units (speed, density, unit pricing)
questions.q: Pack A: 4 yoghurts for £1.60. Pack B: 6 yoghurts for £2.10. Which is better value per yoghurt?
questions.explain: A = 160 ÷ 4 = 40p each. B = 210 ÷ 6 = 35p each. Pack B is cheaper per yoghurt, so it is better value.

questions.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 300 g of rice. How much rice is needed for 6 people?
questions.explain: This is direct proportion. For 1 person: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g. For 6 people: 75 × 6 = 450 g.
